beats.say: A penny gets you a whole music library. And you never see the bill.
Eight CDs for a penny, no commitment listed.
Buy a set number of albums at regular prices later.
If you don't decline, the next selection ships automatically.
Members had to buy a minimum number of albums at regular club prices. Looks like a trap.
But it does a job - a negative-option subscription.
The auto-ship clause forces a shipment unless you actively opt out, turning a penny into a recurring bill.
Revenue hit $1.4 billion in 1996, then collapsed to $17 million by 2014 as the hidden fees disappeared.
You see it everywhere. A gym offers a free trial, then a $30 weekly class pass you must keep.
A café gives a free coffee card, then charges $5 every week unless you cancel.
A streaming app gives a free month, then auto-renews at $9.99 unless you opt out, making the cheap start feel smart.
If something starts with a tiny upfront cost, check what keeps coming after. Follow for more.
